Tuesday, November 17

Game recap

MTL1NYR3Final: MTL 1, NYR 3

The Rangers threw themselves a centennial party at the Garden and Will Cuylle showed up as both the DJ and the bouncer. Montreal actually scored first, Phillip Danault finishing a Lane Hutson and Noah Dobson setup midway through the second, and that lead lasted a whole 1:48 before Cuylle tied it. Then, with 57 seconds left in the period and the Canadiens on a power play, Cuylle scored again, shorthanded, off an Adam Fox feed, which is the hockey version of getting robbed in your own driveway. Scott Morrow added his first of the season in the third, and Joonas Korpisalo did the rest with 24 saves on 25 shots. Jacob Fowler stopped 23 of 26 and deserved a better night. That's three straight wins for New York and two straight losses for Montreal, whose power play just turned a Rangers birthday party into a gift exchange.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN3UTA2Final: VAN 3, UTA 2

Lock the doors, the Canucks have a winning streak. Two whole games. Nikita Tolopilo made his season debut and treated Utah's 36 shots like spam calls, stopping 34 of them, while Vancouver needed only 24 shots of its own to steal a 3-2 win in Salt Lake City. Brock Boeser ran the show with a goal and two assists: he set up Jake DeBrusk's power-play opener, fed Filip Chytil for a 2-1 lead, then buried the winner himself on another power play with 4:23 left. Utah tied it twice in the third, on Vincent Trocheck's power-play goal and Barrett Hayton's equalizer, and Logan Cooley picked up an assist in his return. None of it mattered. Karel Vejmelka gave up three on 24, and the Mammoth are now six games without a win, the last of them to the team in the league's basement. Extinction usually takes longer than this.

Monday, November 16

Game recap

EDM5PHI2Final: EDM 5, PHI 2

The Oilers went to Philadelphia and treated it like a layover. Edmonton won 5-2, scored twice on the power play in the first and led 3-0 after one, with Leon Draisaitl scoring on the first power play and Vasily Podkolzin, unassisted, on the second. Zach Hyman made it 3-0 for his 500th career point. Cole Knuble and Noah Cates got Philly back within 3-2 in the second, and for one intermission it looked like a game. Then Draisaitl scored 1:07 into the third for his 20th goal, and Connor McDavid put the empty-netter away to finish with a goal and two assists and stretch his point streak to 22 games. Tristan Jarry stopped 34 of 36; Dan Vladar stopped 16 of 19. Edmonton is 9-0-1 on the road. The Flyers are still scoring 2.30 goals a game, the fewest in the league, an offense that's been saving its goals like they're for a rainy day.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

FLA1DAL2OTFinal: FLA 1, DAL 2 OT

Florida and Dallas combined for three goals in 63 minutes, and the Stars got the last one. Matthew Tkachuk opened the scoring on a second-period power play for his 700th career point, then Wyatt Johnston tied it under five minutes later. That was it until overtime, when Jason Robertson finished a Roope Hintz feed at 2:56 for his 10th of the year and a 2-1 Stars win. Casey DeSmith stopped 25 of 26 and Akira Schmid 20 of 22. Thomas Harley played 30:54 with Miro Heiskanen out a fifth straight game, which is less a shift pattern than a hostage situation. Brady Tkachuk threw 10 hits and Colin Blackwell matched him, so plenty of people got hit and almost nobody scored. Florida took a point on the second night of a back-to-back and is 2-0-1 this week, but a power play goal and nothing after it is the kind of night that has the Panthers counting the days until Barkov's back.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CGY1ANA6Final: CGY 1, ANA 6

Calgary won in Los Angeles on Saturday and then spent Sunday paying for it in Anaheim, 6-1. Jeff Malott scored 1:16 in, and Cutter Gauthier made it 2-0 later in the first, which means he has now scored in nine straight games, the NHL's longest streak in 29 years and two short of Teemu Selanne's Ducks record. Beckett Sennecke had two goals and an assist, one of them into an empty net, Mikael Granlund added a goal and an assist, and Tim Washe scored too. Mikael Backlund's goal early in the third made it 3-1 for all of 25 seconds before Sennecke answered. Ian Moore got an assist in his season debut. Ville Husso stopped 20 of 21, and Devin Cooley, on the second night of a back-to-back, stopped 28 of 33. The Flames are -23 on the season, a goal differential that reads less like a stat and more like a cry for help.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN6VGK3Final: VAN 6, VGK 3

The last-place Canucks walked into T-Mobile Arena and won 6-3, which is the kind of upset Vegas usually charges admission for. Elias Pettersson scored on a first-period power play and Linus Karlsson and Filip Chytil made it 3-1 by the first intermission. Chytil's first two goals of the season came back to back, the second one shorthanded. Mark Stone's power-play goal early in the third pulled Vegas within 4-3 and tied the Golden Knights' franchise points record at 417, and 24 seconds later Drew O'Connor restored the two-goal lead. Karlsson's empty-netter capped his two-goal night, and Brock Boeser had two assists. Leevi Meriläinen stopped 34 of 37. Carter Hart stopped 21 of 26. Vancouver is still 4-17-1, but Vegas just lost at home to the team everyone else in the league is using as a tune-up, which should be a fun film session.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NSH2SJS4Final: NSH 2, SJS 4

Nashville's seven-game win streak ended in San Jose, against a Sharks team that had played in Utah the night before. Will Smith and Collin Graf scored in the first, Ivar Stenberg made it 3-0 early in the second, and Macklin Celebrini put it away in the third, with Celebrini and Smith each finishing with a goal and two assists. Nils Hoglander and a late Steven Stamkos power-play goal were all the Predators had to show. Alex Nedeljkovic stopped 32 of 34; Juuse Saros stopped 20 of 24. The Sharks have won two in a row and three of their last four, with the kids doing the heavy lifting. Nashville flew all the way to California to remember what losing feels like, courtesy of a Sharks team that's still -18 on the season.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

The Athletic's Josh Yohe writes that Erik Karlsson, 36, is the veteran most likely to leave first and believes he would waive his no-movement clause for a Cup contender. Bryan Rust and Rickard Rakell are both available, and Yohe would be surprised if at least one isn't moved by the March 1 deadline.

Yohe: Crosby's future is 'in his hands,' and the Penguins would trade him or Malkin only if they ask

The Athletic's Josh Yohe reports the Penguins will go along with whatever Sidney Crosby wants when his contract ends after this season, a trade included if he asks for one. Most people in the organization expect him back, though nobody is certain. Evgeni Malkin, 40, can finish the season in Pittsburgh unless he wants out.

Cutter Gauthier's goal streak hits nine games, the NHL's longest in 29 years and two short of Selanne's Ducks record

Gauthier scored again in Sunday's 6-1 win over Calgary and has 16 goals during the streak, plus 20 points in a career-high 11-game point streak. Teemu Selanne's franchise record is 11 straight games, in 1997.

Zach Hyman reaches 500 NHL points as the Oilers win in Philadelphia to go 9-0-1 on the road

Hyman's first-period goal in the 5-2 win was his 500th NHL point. Tristan Jarry made 34 saves as the Flyers went 0-for-8 on the power play, Evan Bouchard passed Charlie Huddy for third in points among Oilers defensemen, and Edmonton has won five straight.

GM John Chayka said Monday that the No. 1 pick's usage is 'right down the fairway' next to other top picks and that the Leafs are doing right by him short and long term. McKenna has six goals and seven assists in 22 games, averaging 13:55 a night.

Jacob Fowler is the early Calder Trophy favorite in NHL.com's quarter-season vote, ahead of Boston's James Hagens

Fowler got 68 voting points in NHL.com's Trophy Tracker, with Bruins forward James Hagens second at 48, Vegas' Trevor Connelly third and Toronto's Gavin McKenna fourth. The Canadiens goalie was 9-1-2 with a 2.13 goals-against average, a .926 save percentage and two shutouts in 12 starts.

Mark Scheifele named NHL First Star of the Week; Wild goalie Jesper Wallstedt is the Second Star

Montreal CanadiensMTL12-5-4 · 28 pts25 shots
1
FinalMadison Square Garden
3
New York RangersNYR13-8-1 · 27 pts26 shots
1st2nd3rdTMTL0101NYR0213

Puckline's Report

The Rangers threw themselves a centennial party at the Garden and Will Cuylle showed up as both the DJ and the bouncer. Montreal actually scored first, Phillip Danault finishing a Lane Hutson and Noah Dobson setup midway through the second, and that lead lasted a whole 1:48 before Cuylle tied it. Then, with 57 seconds left in the period and the Canadiens on a power play, Cuylle scored again, shorthanded, off an Adam Fox feed, which is the hockey version of getting robbed in your own driveway. Scott Morrow added his first of the season in the third, and Joonas Korpisalo did the rest with 24 saves on 25 shots. Jacob Fowler stopped 23 of 26 and deserved a better night. That's three straight wins for New York and two straight losses for Montreal, whose power play just turned a Rangers birthday party into a gift exchange.

By Puckline Prince

1st2nd3rdTVAN0123UTA0022

Puckline's Report

Lock the doors, the Canucks have a winning streak. Two whole games. Nikita Tolopilo made his season debut and treated Utah's 36 shots like spam calls, stopping 34 of them, while Vancouver needed only 24 shots of its own to steal a 3-2 win in Salt Lake City. Brock Boeser ran the show with a goal and two assists: he set up Jake DeBrusk's power-play opener, fed Filip Chytil for a 2-1 lead, then buried the winner himself on another power play with 4:23 left. Utah tied it twice in the third, on Vincent Trocheck's power-play goal and Barrett Hayton's equalizer, and Logan Cooley picked up an assist in his return. None of it mattered. Karel Vejmelka gave up three on 24, and the Mammoth are now six games without a win, the last of them to the team in the league's basement. Extinction usually takes longer than this.

LAK @ BOS · 7:00 PM ET

Los Angeles KingsLAK5-11-2 · 12 PTSML +138
@7:00 PM ETTue Nov 17 · TD Garden
LAK +138MLBOS -166
Boston BruinsBOS13-6-1 · 27 PTSML -166

Puckline Preview

The Kings spent Monday practicing at Harvard, which is fitting, because their season so far reads like a rejection letter. Los Angeles is 5-11-2, has lost four straight (all at home, somehow) and went 2-5-0 on the homestand it just escaped. Now it opens a four-game trip in a building owned by a team that already beat it 4-1 in October, back when the Kings were 0-4-2 and still looking for Peter Laviolette's first win. Leading scorer Artemi Panarin is still away from the team for a family matter and is expected to miss a second straight game, Erik Gustafsson is back after missing three, and Darcy Kuemper is carrying an .872 save percentage around like a parking ticket.

Boston has its own homework. The Bruins won four straight, then got run out of their own rink twice, 5-2 by Montreal and 6-2 by Minnesota, and Marco Sturm responded by reshuffling the lineup: Mason Lohrei is back in after his first healthy scratch of the season, Sean Kuraly takes Matthew Poitras' spot, and Michael DiPietro gets the net instead of Jeremy Swayman. The Kings have scored three goals in their last three games against Boston. The Bruins have allowed 11 in their last two. Something has to give, and both sides would very much like it to be the other guy.

By Puckline Prince

EDM @ FLA · 7:00 PM ET

Edmonton OilersEDM16-3-3 · 35 PTSML +106
@7:00 PM ETTue Nov 17 · Amerant Bank Arena
EDM +106MLFLA -128
Florida PanthersFLA12-7-3 · 27 PTSML -128

Puckline Preview

Edmonton returns to Sunrise, the place where two of its Junes went to die. The Panthers beat the Oilers in the 2024 and 2025 Stanley Cup Finals, and the regular season hasn't been much kinder: Edmonton has lost five of the last six meetings since November 2023. The Oilers show up as the best team in hockey anyway, 16-3-3 with five straight wins and a 9-0-1 road record. Connor McDavid has a point in all 22 games, 53 of them in total, and the Oilers' own preview says one more tonight ties Wayne Gretzky's 1988-89 start for the fourth-longest season-opening streak ever. Leon Draisaitl got to 20 goals before anyone else and has points in nine straight. Devon Levi and Tristan Jarry have been trading starts and wins.

Florida is 12-7-3 and has done all of that without its captain. Aleksander Barkov hasn't played a game this season; he skated again this morning and is close, but not tonight: Paul Maurice says the doctors look at him and Brad Marchand, who is also still out, on Thursday. Matthew Tkachuk has points in eight straight and just hit 700 for his career, his brother Brady is on his wing now because apparently one wasn't annoying enough, and Jacob Markstrom has stopped 62 of 64 in his last two starts. McDavid has the streak. Florida has the rings. Only one of those travels well in this building.

By Puckline Prince

CBJ @ NYI · 7:00 PM ET

Columbus Blue JacketsCBJ7-11-0 · 14 PTSML +114
@7:00 PM ETTue Nov 17 · UBS Arena
CBJ +114MLNYI -137
New York IslandersNYI9-6-4 · 22 PTSML -137

Puckline Preview

The last time Columbus walked into UBS Arena, in March, it brought a 12-game point streak and left with a 1-0 loss, a Bo Horvat goal 85 seconds in and 26 Ilya Sorokin saves being all the Islanders needed. The Blue Jackets would kill for a 12-game anything right now. They are 7-11-0, last in the East, losers of four straight and 1-5-0 on the road, and this is the first stop of a four-game trip. Sean Monahan and Conor Garland stayed home hurt, Don Granato is running the bench again with Rick Bowness still away from the team, and the goalie math finally won an argument: Jet Greaves is 2-8-0, Cam Talbot is 5-3-0, and Talbot is expected to get the net tonight. Kent Johnson, with 13 points in his last 10 games, is doing what he can.

The Islanders come home from California 2-0-1 and on a four-game point streak. Simon Holmstrom just had his first career hat trick and has five goals in four games, Mathew Barzal made his season debut Saturday with an assist, and rookie Matthew Schaefer had three helpers in the same game. The one soft spot: New York is 1-2-2 in its last five at home. If the Islanders can't hold serve against a team that has two regulation wins all season, the Long Island Rail Road is going to hear about it.

By Puckline Prince

BUF @ PHI · 7:00 PM ET

Buffalo SabresBUF8-8-4 · 20 PTSML -132
@7:00 PM ETTue Nov 17 · Xfinity Mobile Arena
BUF -132MLPHI +110
Philadelphia FlyersPHI6-11-6 · 18 PTSML +110

Puckline Preview

Somebody has to score in this game. Probably. Buffalo hasn't scored in its last five periods, has six goals during a four-game winless slide and is shooting 5.7 percent in that stretch, which is less a slump than a vow of silence. Alex Lyon said the Sabres are 'on a precipice', and Lindy Ruff spent Monday shuffling everything that wasn't bolted down: Jiri Kulich, with one goal in 12 games, is back at center on the top line, the power play got new faces, and Lyon himself is expected to make a third straight start.

The good news for Buffalo is the opponent. Philadelphia scores 2.30 goals a game, bottom of the league, and went 0-for-8 on the power play Sunday against Edmonton while the home crowd chanted 'Fire Tocchet', which in Philadelphia counts as constructive feedback. Rick Tocchet says the room is still close after Matvei Michkov and Nick Seeler had words on the bench in Edmonton, and the front office reportedly told Michkov to his face that he isn't going anywhere. The Flyers did win the first meeting, 3-1 in Buffalo on Oct. 21, and are 1-3-1 in their last five at home. Two teams, one working offense between them, and that's being generous.

By Puckline Prince

OTT @ WPG · 7:00 PM ET

Ottawa SenatorsOTT13-6-2 · 28 PTSML -134
@7:00 PM ETTue Nov 17 · Canada Life Centre
OTT -134MLWPG +112
Winnipeg JetsWPG10-8-3 · 23 PTSML +112

Puckline Preview

Three weeks ago the Jets couldn't buy a win: nine straight games without one. Now they can't lose. Winnipeg has won six in a row, hung eight on Dallas, and on Saturday spotted Chicago a 4-0 lead before winning 5-4 in a shootout, the kind of comeback that says as much about the Blackhawks as it does about the Jets. Mark Scheifele passed Dale Hawerchuk for the franchise points record along the way and was named one of the league's three stars of the week, and Kyle Connor is back on his wing after a maintenance day Monday. The catch: Stuart Skinner's .880 save percentage suggests the streak has been built on outscoring problems, not solving them.

Ottawa is quietly just as hot, 4-0-1 in its last five and tied for first in the Atlantic on points at 13-6-2. Linus Ullmark has won both starts since coming back, the second his 200th career win. The Senators are thin up front, though, with Nick Cousins, Andre Burakovsky and Hayden Hodgson all out, so Tyler Boucher, the 10th pick in 2021, got his first NHL recall and makes his NHL debut tonight. Five years is a long wait for a first shift. Ottawa won both meetings last season. This is the first of this season, and neither team remembers how to lose.

By Puckline Prince

WSH @ TBL · 7:30 PM ET

Washington CapitalsWSH10-8-0 · 20 PTSML +134
@7:30 PM ETTue Nov 17 · Benchmark International Arena
WSH +134MLTBL -162
Tampa Bay LightningTBL13-5-2 · 28 PTSML -162

Puckline Preview

John Carlson played more than 1,000 games as a Washington Capital. Tonight he lines up against them in a Lightning sweater, fresh off a five-point night in Buffalo that pushed him past 800 career points. Breakups are easier when your ex isn't thriving. The Capitals, meanwhile, just lost both ends of a home-and-home to New Jersey, 5-2 and 7-4, after leading early in both, and the defense that was the league's stingiest at 5-on-5 through 18 games last season (24 goals against) has already given up 42. Rasmus Sandin and Vincent Desharnais are on the trip but still in noncontact jerseys, so help is not walking through that door tonight.

Tampa Bay sits first in the Atlantic at 13-5-2 and is annoyed: Detroit shut the Lightning out 2-0 on Saturday to end their home win streak. Reinforcements are coming: Brayden Point came off injured reserve today and is expected to play, while Anthony Cirelli and Erik Cernak skated this morning and are game-time decisions. Tampa won the first meeting 3-1 on Oct. 3 and has taken the last four from Washington. Logan Thompson and Andrei Vasilevskiy are the projected goalies, and both arrive with save percentages under .890, so nobody in this one should be bragging.

By Puckline Prince

TOR @ CHI · 7:30 PM ET

Toronto Maple LeafsTOR8-12-2 · 18 PTSML -142
@7:30 PM ETTue Nov 17 · United Center
TOR -142MLCHI +118
Chicago BlackhawksCHI5-13-2 · 12 PTSML +118

Puckline Preview

The Maple Leafs are finally leaving Toronto, and not a moment too soon. They went 0-6 on a homestand that was supposed to fix things, got outscored 23-9, and capped it with a 1-0 loss to Edmonton in which John Tavares' tying goal was wiped out for a high stick. Six straight regulation losses have them 8-12-2 and last in the Atlantic. Jim Hiller says they 'deserved better', GM John Chayka calls the results 'unacceptable' while backing his coach, and Sergei Bobrovsky has an .881 save percentage and Chayka's 'benefit of the doubt', which is what you give a goalie when you can't give him back. Hiller is giving him the net tonight, too. Morgan Rielly is likely to return on defense.

If there is a get-right game on the schedule, it's this one. Chicago is 5-13-2 with a minus-37 goal differential, and on Saturday it led Winnipeg 4-0 at home and lost in a shootout. That is hard to do on purpose. Patrick Kane is back and just passed Dale Hawerchuk for 23rd on the all-time points list, Connor Bedard is still worth the ticket, and Bowen Byram will miss a 14th straight game. The last time these two met, last December, the Blackhawks blew a 2-0 third-period lead in Toronto. One of these teams is going to feel better about itself by 10 o'clock, and it will be a strange feeling for either.

By Puckline Prince

ANA @ STL · 8:00 PM ET

Anaheim DucksANA11-9-1 · 23 PTSML +110
@8:00 PM ETTue Nov 17 · Enterprise Center
ANA +110MLSTL -132
St Louis BluesSTL9-9-2 · 20 PTSML -132

Puckline Preview

Cutter Gauthier has scored in nine straight games, the longest goal streak the NHL has seen in 29 years, and he's two away from Teemu Selanne's Ducks record of 11. He has 18 goals and a league-best 10 on the power play. Here's the problem: St. Louis has killed 15 straight Anaheim power plays over the last four meetings. Here's the opening: Joel Hofer and his .922 save percentage get the night off, and Jordan Binnington, making his first start since Nov. 5, brings an .849. Something is getting broken tonight, the streak or the kill.

There's a reunion in it too. Mason McTavish faces the Ducks for the first time since they traded him to St. Louis, and he gets to see what he left behind: rookie Beckett Sennecke with 12 goals and 26 points in 21 games, and a team that scores 3.76 a night. What he also left behind is the goaltending. Lukas Dostal is sitting on an .856 and Ville Husso, who beat Calgary on Sunday and is projected to start again, on an .880, which is how a team with that offense is only 11-9-1. The Blues are 9-9-2, have scored eight goals in their last five home games and lost 4-1 to Florida on Saturday, though Philip Broberg and Jake Neighbours are both playing after scares. St. Louis has scored four or more in seven of the last eight meetings. Against those save percentages, the Blues' offense might finally find the pulse it's been looking for.

By Puckline Prince

NSH @ MIN · 8:00 PM ET

Nashville PredatorsNSH11-5-5 · 27 PTSML +172
@8:00 PM ETTue Nov 17 · Grand Casino Arena
NSH +172MLMIN -210
Minnesota WildMIN15-3-4 · 34 PTSML -210

Puckline Preview

The season started with these two on opening night in Nashville, a 3-1 Wild win with Blake Coleman scoring the winner in his Minnesota debut and a Predators goal waved off for goalie interference. Seven weeks later it's a matchup of two of the hottest teams in the Central. Minnesota is 15-3-4 and hasn't lost in regulation in 11 games; Kirill Kaprizov and Quinn Hughes each have a point in every one of them. The Wild have won eight straight on the road, so naturally they come home, where they haven't played since Nov. 7. Jesper Wallstedt is 14-2-3 with a .926 save percentage and a 1.94 goals-against average, numbers that look like a typo, and Brock Faber is back in the lineup. GM Bill Guerin has even said the Wild could keep Hughes past the deadline without an extension, which is the kind of thing you say when you're 15-3-4.

Nashville had won seven in a row before San Jose, of all teams, ended it Sunday. This is the Predators' fifth straight road game (3-1-0 so far), Steven Stamkos has 12 goals, Juuse Saros has a .917, and Jonathan Marchessault returns tonight after missing seven games. Three of the four meetings last season went to overtime. The Predators already have five overtime and shootout losses on the books this season, so if this one goes long, Nashville has seen that movie before.

By Puckline Prince

DAL @ VGK · 10:00 PM ET

Dallas StarsDAL12-6-2 · 26 PTSML +100
@10:00 PM ETTue Nov 17 · T-Mobile Arena
DAL +100MLVGK -120
Vegas Golden KnightsVGK13-6-3 · 29 PTSML -120

Puckline Preview

These two have settled things in the playoffs twice in the last four springs, Vegas in six in the 2023 conference final and Dallas in seven in the 2024 first round, and they get each other twice this week, tonight and Thursday, both on the Strip. The Golden Knights could use the distraction. On Sunday they lost 6-3 at home to a Vancouver team that walked in with three wins and a seven-game losing streak, the hockey equivalent of losing your wallet to the worst pickpocket in town. The upside: Mark Stone's goal in that game was his 417th point with Vegas, tying Jonathan Marchessault's franchise record, so his next one makes him the Golden Knights' all-time leader. Tomas Hertl has points in seven straight. Noah Hanifin is out.

Dallas arrives 12-6-2 after sweeping a weekend back-to-back, a 2-0 shutout of Buffalo in which Jamie Benn got his 1,000th point and a 2-1 overtime win over Florida on a Jason Robertson goal. The blue line gets its best player back, and loses another body. Miro Heiskanen is expected to return after missing five straight, but Lian Bichsel is on injured reserve and Tyler Myers, who left Sunday's game early, is out, which is how Thomas Harley ended up playing 30:54. All three meetings last season were one-goal games. Expect more of the same, and expect Harley to sleep well on Friday.

By Puckline Prince

CGY @ SJS · 10:00 PM ET

Calgary FlamesCGY9-11-1 · 19 PTSML +110
@10:00 PM ETTue Nov 17 · SAP Center at San Jose
CGY +110MLSJS -132
San Jose SharksSJS10-11-2 · 22 PTSML -132

Puckline Preview

Calgary was just here. On Nov. 2 the Flames won 2-1 in San Jose behind 26 saves from Dustin Wolf, who treats the Sharks like a personal savings account: NHL.com had him 11-2-0 against them for his career after that one. Calgary has taken four of the last five meetings. That's the good news. The bad news is the rest of it: a 6-1 loss in Anaheim on Sunday on the back half of a back-to-back, an offense scoring 2.43 goals a game, and Jonathan Huberdeau still not on the trip: the Flames sent him to the AHL Wranglers on a conditioning loan today, so his season debut waits a little longer.

San Jose is the better story right now. The Sharks are 3-0-1 in their last four and just ended Nashville's seven-game win streak, with Macklin Celebrini and Will Smith putting up three points apiece. Celebrini has 27 points and tied Dale Hawerchuk for the fifth-most three-point games before age 21, which is the sort of sentence that makes the rest of the Pacific nervous. The fine print: three of those last four games went to a shootout, and only three of San Jose's 10 wins have come in regulation. The Sharks don't beat you so much as outlast you. Kiefer Sherwood, who left Sunday's game, is week to week with an upper-body injury, Alexander Wennberg returns after missing two games, and Brett Leason is up from the Barracuda. Calgary can't score, San Jose can't finish in 60. Bring a snack.

By Puckline Prince
